Second reading of a flat table. arabidopsis.Rd (spaMM 4.7.17): 948 accessions 'from European Arabidopsis thaliana populations' with their genotypes at four SNPs (Fournier-Level et al. 2011) and 13 climatic variables (Hancock et al. 2011). Its example fits fitme(cbind(pos1046738,1-pos1046738)~seasonal+Matern(1|LAT+LONG), family=binomial(), method='PQL/L', data=arabidopsis), 'The response is binary', first with rho, nu and lambda fixed at values 'deduced from the following fit', then estimated (Rousset and Ferdy 2014). LAT and LONG identify the collection sites, many holding several accessions with the same climatic values, and the Matern random effect takes one value per distinct location, so LAT:LONG is the grouping factor, as pymc_examples gambia_dataset's x:y; the first reading's coordinate rule covers coordinates each row holds once (besag.checks). pos5510910, pos6235221 and pos8132698 are the other SNPs, no model of the page; the other climatic variables are unused.
